## Congratulations!

You completed **Agent Orchestration in the GitHub Copilot CLI**. :tada:

In this exercise, you practiced a terminal-first orchestration workflow from a Codespace. You used GitHub Copilot CLI to work through each artifact and document how an Orchestrator coordinates specialist agents.

## What you learned

You learned how to:

- Use GitHub Copilot CLI in a Codespace terminal.
- Map the Orchestrator, Planner, Coder, and Designer roles to their target models.
- Create a Planner handoff before implementation begins.
- Convert planned work into phases and specialist assignments.
- Separate parallel work from sequential work.
- Prevent file conflicts with explicit file scopes.
- Write a final Orchestrator report with validation notes.

## What's next?

- Try this orchestration pattern on a real feature in one of your repositories.
- Use `/agent`, `/model`, `/tasks`, and `/fleet` in GitHub Copilot CLI to explore agent and subagent workflows.
- Add repository instructions that explain when to use Planner, Coder, Designer, and Orchestrator roles.
- Explore [GitHub Codespaces dev containers](https://docs.github.com/en/codespaces/setting-up-your-project-for-codespaces/introduction-to-dev-containers) for repeatable CLI-first environments.
- Learn more about [GitHub Copilot CLI](https://docs.github.com/copilot/concepts/agents/about-copilot-cli).
